feature: hexa status says where the work stands
description: `hexa status` reports git ahead/behind/dirty against the last-fetched upstream, opt-in remote reachability that never fakes success, this session's loop state and other live sessions, an accurate doc comment, and the same fields as --json.

specs.description: A local commit ahead of the fetched upstream is counted and the line says the count is as of the last fetch.
specs.given: a temp repo whose branch main tracks origin/main on a bare upstream, with one local commit not pushed
specs.then: the git line reads `ahead 1, behind 0 of origin/main, as of the last fetch`

specs.description: Modified and untracked files appear in the dirty counts with their paths.
specs.given: a repo with upstream, one tracked file `a.txt` modified and unstaged, and one new untracked file `b.txt`
specs.then: the output shows 1 modified, 0 staged and 1 untracked, and lists `a.txt` and `b.txt`

specs.description: Staged changes are counted separately from modified ones.
specs.given: a repo with one file changed and added to the index, and nothing else dirty
specs.then: the output shows 1 staged and 0 modified, and lists the staged path

specs.description: A branch with no upstream is said, not omitted, and no ahead/behind numbers are made up.
specs.given: a repo whose current branch has no upstream configured
specs.then: a git line is present and says the branch has no upstream; it shows no ahead or behind count and no `up to date` claim

specs.description: When more than ten paths are dirty, the counts are shown but the paths are not listed.
specs.given: a repo with eleven untracked files
specs.then: the output shows 11 untracked and does not list the eleven paths

specs.description: A clean tree is reported as clean, not left out.
specs.given: a repo with upstream and no modified, staged or untracked files
specs.then: the output says the tree is clean (or shows zero counts) rather than leaving out the dirty-tree report

specs.description: For every repo state, the git section is present, and ahead/behind match git's count against the recorded upstream ref.
specs.given: any repo with any combination of upstream present or absent, commits ahead or behind, and dirty files
specs.then: the git section is always present. If an upstream exists, ahead and behind equal `git rev-list --left-right --count @{u}...HEAD` and the line names the upstream and says `as of the last fetch`. If none exists, the line says so. The modified, staged and untracked counts equal those from `git status --porcelain`. Paths are listed exactly when the dirty total is ten or fewer.

specs.description: With --remote and an unreachable upstream, status says unreachable, gives the error's first line, and still exits 0.
specs.given: a repo whose upstream remote URL points to an address that refuses connections
specs.then: the remote line says unreachable, followed by the first line of the git error, and the process exits with status 0

specs.description: With --remote and a reachable upstream, reachability is reported as reachable.
specs.given: a repo whose upstream is a reachable bare repository
specs.then: the remote line says the upstream is reachable

specs.description: Without --remote, the line says reachability was not checked.
specs.given: any repo with an upstream
specs.then: the remote line says reachability was not checked

specs.description: Status never fetches, so the remote-tracking refs are unchanged, even with --remote.
specs.given: a repo whose bare upstream has gained a commit since the last fetch, and whose recorded origin/main ref has a known hash
specs.then: the origin/main ref has the same hash as before, behind stays 0, and FETCH_HEAD is not created or modified

specs.description: An unreachable remote is never reported as up to date or reachable, and the line is not left out.
specs.given: a repo whose upstream refuses connections and whose last fetch matched HEAD
specs.then: the output does not say `up to date` or `reachable` for the remote; it says unreachable

specs.description: An upstream that hangs does not hang status; the short timeout ends the check and it is reported as unreachable.
specs.given: a repo whose upstream URL points to a host that accepts the connection but never answers
specs.then: the command finishes within the short timeout plus a small margin, says unreachable with a timeout reason, and exits 0

specs.description: For every remote state, the reachability line is present and never claims more than was checked.
specs.given: any repo, with `--remote` given or not, and an upstream that is reachable, refuses, times out or is absent
specs.then: a reachability line is always present. Without `--remote` it says not checked. With `--remote` it says reachable only when `git ls-remote --exit-code` succeeded within the timeout; otherwise it says unreachable with the error's first line. The exit status is 0 in every case. No remote-tracking ref changes.

specs.description: A loop entry with a gate, tasks and a kept last_run shows all three, plus the ADR and stage.
specs.given: this session's loop entry names an ADR and a stage, has a gate, has 5 tasks with 2 done and the third as current task, and has a `last_run` kept under ADR-2611020815
specs.then: the loop section shows the ADR, the stage, the gate, `2 of 5 done`, the current task, and the `last_run`

specs.description: Other live sessions get one line each, in the form the hooks print.
specs.given: this session plus two other live sessions with loop entries
specs.then: exactly two extra lines appear, one per other session, each in the same format the hooks print for that session

specs.description: With no kept gate, no last_run line is made up.
specs.given: this session's loop entry has a gate and tasks but no `last_run`
specs.then: the loop section shows the gate and task progress and shows no `last_run` value

specs.description: This session's loop state is not taken from another session.
specs.given: this session has no loop entry, and another live session has one with a gate
specs.then: the loop section does not show the other session's ADR, gate or tasks as this session's; the other session appears only as its one line

specs.description: For every set of loop entries, this session's fields are reported from its own entry and every other live session gets exactly one line.
specs.given: any set of live sessions, with any mix of ADR, stage, gate, tasks and last_run present or absent
specs.then: this session's ADR, stage, gate, `n of m done` and current task match its loop entry, where n is the done count and m the total. `last_run` appears exactly when the entry keeps one. The number of other-session lines equals the number of other live sessions.

specs.description: The doc comment says what the command does.
specs.given: the source of the status command
specs.when: its doc comment, and the help text built from it, is read
specs.then: it describes reporting git ahead/behind/dirty state, optional remote reachability, and loop state

specs.description: The doc comment and help do not promise service health.
specs.given: the built hexa-cli binary and the status command source
specs.when: `hexa status --help` is read and the doc comment is inspected
specs.then: neither contains `service health` nor any claim to check services

specs.description: --json emits the git, remote and loop fields as one parseable JSON value.
specs.given: a repo one commit ahead, with one modified file, no `--remote`, and a loop entry with gate, tasks and last_run
specs.then: stdout parses as a single JSON value carrying ahead 1, behind 0, the upstream name, the dirty counts with paths, remote not checked, and the loop ADR, stage, gate, task progress, current task and last_run

specs.description: --json does not silently drop states. No upstream and unreachable remote are explicit values, not missing keys.
specs.given: a repo with no upstream, and separately a repo whose upstream is unreachable, with `--remote --json`
specs.then: the JSON states no upstream explicitly, and states unreachable with the error's first line. Neither state is shown by leaving a key out or by writing a value that reads as up to date.

specs.description: --json output holds only JSON; no human-readable text is mixed into stdout.
specs.given: any repo
specs.then: the whole of stdout parses as JSON, with no leading or trailing text lines

specs.description: For every state, the JSON carries the same facts as the text output.
specs.given: any repo and loop state, with `--remote` given or not
specs.when: `hexa status` and `hexa status --json` are run on the same state
specs.then: every fact in the text output is in the JSON with the same value, and the JSON adds no fact the text lacks: ahead, behind, upstream or no upstream, as-of-last-fetch, dirty counts and listed paths, reachability, loop fields, last_run and other sessions
